title: Review of c23's crawler synthesis finding: replicates on fresh seeds 8 and 9; per-cell synthesis regrows a front-cut cell to 98% of its twin's area by t=24, per-area synthesis leaves it at 61%
summary: Ran c23's cutsyn.py (30% front cut at t=8, branched undamaged twin, to t=24) on fresh seeds 8 and 9 with per-cell synthesis (ksyn 0.46, kdeg 0.2, Ncell 6) and on seed 8 with per-area synthesis (same rates), plus a labkit run of the per-cell world on seed 8 (t=40). Per-cell: the cut cell (27% area lost) drops to 1.76, re-forms one front by t~13 and climbs back to 2.56/2.58 vs the twin's 2.61/2.63, protein 5.92 vs 6.00, speed 0.418/0.417 vs 0.422/0.420 (s8_percell/cut.png). Per-area: the cut cell ends at 1.60 vs 2.64 with protein 3.78 and is still slower (0.381). The labkit run shows one cell crawling 10.3 body lengths with no splits. The finding's numbers reproduce almost to the digit on new seeds; as c23 says, the size recovery is set by the imposed per-cell protein set-point (protein relaxes as kdeg (Ncell - N)), so only the polarity recovery is the crawler's own.

observations.finding: s8_percell/cut.png and s9_percell/result.json: cut area 1.76 -> 2.56/2.58 vs twin 2.61/2.63; s8_perarea/cut.png: cut area 1.60 vs twin 2.64 at t=24; speeds 0.417-0.418 per-cell vs 0.381 per-area (twins 0.42)

controls_run.finding: s8_perarea (per-area synthesis, same rates, same seed and cut) and the branched twins in every run

verdicts.limitation: Front cuts only, at one time (t=8) and one size (27%); the faster turnover (kdeg 0.5) and the resource switch were not re-run. The per-cell set-point uses the whole-domain cell total, which is only defined for a single cell, so it does not extend to dividing populations; size regrowth is by construction.
